Mumbai: Moshe Holtzberg, the Israeli boy popularly known as ‘Baby Moshe’, who survived the 2008 Nariman House terror attack in which his parents were killed, is pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and aspires to become a rabbi like his father.

Rabbi Israel Kozlovsky, who is in charge of Nariman House, one of the places targeted by Pakistani Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists during the November 26, 2008 attacks, said he met Moshe two weeks ago at a rabbinical conference in New York.

“The conference was attended by 4,000 to 5,000 rabbis from across the world, and Moshe was also present,” Kozlovsky said, showing a photograph on his mobile phone of Moshe posing in traditional attire alongside other rabbis.
A rabbi is a spiritual leader, religious teacher and legal scholar.
In the photograph, the once two-year-old ‘Baby Moshe’, whose footage of sobbing inconsolably after the attack drew global attention and moved millions, appears as a 20-year-old man.
“He is currently pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and wants to become a rabbi.
Hopefully, he will return to India.
That is our hope,” Kozlovsky told PTI on Wednesday.
Moshe’s parents, Rabbi Gavriel Holtzberg and Rivka Holtzberg, were killed when terrorists stormed the Chabad House, a centre that served the Jewish community here.
Moshe’s nanny, Sandra Samuel, rescued him from the building and fled.
He later moved to Israel to stay with his grandparents.

article_sentences: The Indian and Chinese armies held high-level talks this month in the Arunachal Pradesh sector focusing on border management and addressing outstanding issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

The talks, believed to have spread over a number of days, were held amid reports of aggressive military posturing by Chinese troops along the frontier, especially in the Upper Subansiri region of Arunachal Pradesh.
In September too, the senior military commanders of the two armies were engaged in flag talks in two sessions on both sides of the frontier in the Arunachal Pradesh sector.

“India and China engage regularly through diplomatic and military mechanisms and you are well aware of those mechanisms,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at his regular media briefing while responding to a question.
“A meeting of the senior military commanders was held in the eastern sector recently.
Discussions between the two sides focused on improving border management as well as addressing outstanding issues along the LAC,” he said.
Mr. Jaiswal said such interactions are aimed at maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas and preventing any escalation.

Lt. Gen Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of the Army’s III Corps headquartered near Dimapur in Nagaland, led the Indian delegation at the talks in the second week of this month, while the Chinese side was led by his counterpart.

In the military and diplomatic talks, India has been conveying to the Chinese side the importance of maintaining peace and tranquillity in the frontier regions for the continued development and progress of the overall bilateral relationship.

In the last one-and-a-half years, the two sides have taken a series of measures to rebuild their relationship after it came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in eastern Ladakh in 2020.

Nearly 50,000 troops of the Indian Army are deployed in various mountainous locations in eastern Ladakh, as multiple rounds of talks between the two sides have not yielded a concrete outcome to de-escalate the situation.
China has also deployed an equal number of troops, according to officials.

opening: New Delhi, Nov 26: The Centre on Thursday informed the Delhi High Court that a Look Out Circular (LOC) had been issued against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das, who has challenged the authorities' decision to prevent him from travelling to London to attend an event at the University of Oxford.

Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Centre, told a single-judge Bench of Justice Amit Mahajan that discrepancies detected in Das's passport could also have implications for his Indian citizenship.
body: The Centre’s law officer submitted that the discrepancies in the passport were being examined by the authorities and that an LOC had been issued against the activist.
However, senior advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for Das, told the High Court that he had not been informed about the issuance of any LOC against him.

The submissions came during the hearing of Das's plea challenging the action of the authorities in stopping him at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport when he was scheduled to travel to London.
The development comes a day after the Delhi High Court declined to entertain an urgent mentioning of the matter before Acting Chief Justice (ACJ) Nitin Wasudeo Sambre.

Das's counsel had sought an immediate hearing, submitting that his flight to the United Kingdom was scheduled for Thursday evening and that the petition could become infructuous if not taken up urgently.
The counsel had told the High Court that Das was stopped at immigration, but no order or LOC restricting his overseas travel was shown to him.
However, the Acting Chief Justice declined the request for an urgent hearing on Wednesday and said the matter would be taken up on Thursday.

Meanwhile, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) had said on Wednesday that the Regional Passport Office (RPO) in Chennai issued a show-cause notice to Das on November 23, seeking clarification regarding his place of birth.
MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, during a bi-weekly media briefing, said Das had also been advised not to use his passport until he submitted his response to the notice.
Jaiswal said that a show-cause notice is issued when authorities detect discrepancies in a passport application and seek an explanation from the applicant.
The controversy erupted after Das claimed on social media that he had been stopped at the Delhi airport from travelling to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford.
However, the Delhi BJP disputed his version, maintaining that Das was scheduled to attend an event organised by the Oxford Union and not deliver a lecture at the university.

stories.title: Public confidence in judicial authority must be continuously earned: CJI
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Thursday said a confident institution must have the capacity to engage with criticism without treating every disagreement as a challenge to its authority, underlining that disagreement is not a weakness of a constitutional democracy. Addressing a Constitution Day function organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) at the apex court lawns, the CJI also said that the Constitution is not tested only during extraordinary political or institutional crises, but it is tested every day. The proposed rates for China and Vietnam under trade agreements are 20 percent, while Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia and Thailand face 18 percent.The US currently imposes an additional 10 percent tariff on many Indian goods, apart from regular customs duties. The proposed tariff would not be added on top of existing tariffs. Instead, the USTR has proposed calculating the rate net of certain existing duties under Section 301 of the Trade Act, while also considering adjustments for other tariffs, including those imposed under Section 232 (which allows the US to impose tariffs on specific products on national security grounds). These already apply to products such as steel, aluminium, automobiles, patented pharmaceutical articles and semiconductors.Responding to the notice, India's Ministry of Commerce said it was examining the findings. It argued that these policies "target exports and export-led growth" without commensurately promoting domestic demand and consumption, distort fair, market-oriented competition and undermine worker and public welfare.India's manufacturing sector accounted for an average 13.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) between 2021 and 2025, compared with 9.9 percent in the US and a global average of 15.4 percent. Investment averaged 34 percent of GDP in India over the period, against 21.6 percent in the US and 26.6 percent globally.Manufacturing accounted for 28.6 percent of labour income in India in 2022, compared with 47.8 percent in the US and 41.5 percent across Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) economies. The USTR also referred to an International Monetary Fund (IMF) assessment that 15 percent of continuously operating firms in India were zombie firms, or companies that remain in business despite persistently weak financial performance.Steel, solar, health and information and communications technology (ICT) were among the sectors the USTR examined, with the report arguing that India's policies in these areas have contributed to structural excess capacity. It said India had increasingly used industrial policies to expand manufacturing and production in these sectors, particularly those with export potential.The investigation concluded that India's acts, policies and practices burden or restrict US commerce by "reducing commercial opportunities for US producers and exporters in India and third-country markets" and "increase US economic security risks, including through reliance on NME inputs".The US trade office also pointed to India's trade surplus with the US, which stood at $57.3 billion in 2025. article_sentences: Guwahati: The Supreme Court of India on Thursday, November 26, 2026, directed the Union Government and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to introduce separate red hexagonal warning labels on packaged foods high in fat, sugar and salt.
The ruling, delivered in New Delhi, aims to strengthen consumer awareness and protect public health through clearer front-of-pack nutrition labelling.
A Division Bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran rejected the approach of using one combined warning symbol for multiple nutrients of concern.
The court directed FSSAI to ensure that every nutrient receives its own clearly identifiable warning.
The judgment states, "The authority shall ensure that the FOPNL provides for a separate hexagon for each nutrient of concern...
rather than a single combined hexagon."
Under the direction, the front of packaged food products must display individual red hexagonal labels identifying HIGH FAT, HIGH SUGAR and HIGH SALT, depending on their nutritional composition.
The ruling replaces the regulator's August 2026 proposal, which had suggested a combined warning label.
The Supreme Court's decision followed a public interest litigation filed by 3S and Our Health Society, represented by advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi.
The petitioner sought stronger front-of-pack nutrition labelling to help consumers identify packaged foods containing high levels of fat, sugar and salt.
The court also addressed the nutritional thresholds proposed under Table 15.1 of the Dietary Guidelines for Indians (DGI) 2024.
The Bench said these nutritional values should not be adopted without modification because they account for added sugars and fats rather than total sugars and fats.

stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 26 : The 8th National Security Advisor Level Meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC), held in the Maldives, reaffirmed the collective commitment of member states to promote regional peace and security through sustained cooperation. A joint statement issued on Thursday following the meeting said that the CSC member states, including Maldives, India, Mauritius (virtual) and Sri Lanka, signed the Agreed Minutes and adopted the Roadmap of Cooperation for 2026–2027. The roadmap outlined key deliverables and planned activities under the five pillars of cooperation, namely Maritime Safety and Security; Countering Terrorism and Radicalisation; Combating Trafficking and Transnational Organised Crime; Cyber Security and Protection of Critical Infrastructure and Technology; and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief. “Member States placed emphasis on strengthening collaboration across the five pillars of cooperation, particularly through training, sharing best practices and capacity-building initiatives, while underlining the importance of continued collective efforts towards advancing the objectives of the Colombo Security Conclave," read the statement. The high-level delegations were led by Lt. Col. (Retd.) Ibrahim Latheef, National Security Advisor of the Maldives; Ajit Doval, National Security Advisor to the Prime Minister of India; Sampath Thuyacontha, Secretary, Ministry of Defence of Sri Lanka; and Lieutenant General Faizur Rahman, Commandant, National Defence College of Bangladesh. Australia and Malaysia participated as Guests. Australia was represented by Sarah Storey, First Assistant Secretary, South and Southeast Asia Group and Head of the Office of Southeast Asia in the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. Malaysia was represented by Khairul Azhar (Nik) bin Abu Bakar, Director from the Maritime Security and Sovereignty Division at the National Security Council at the Prime Minister’s Department. During the meeting on Wednesday, the first Secretary General of the CSC, Vice Admiral S.N. Ghormade (retd) presented a comprehensive review of the actions undertaken to implement the decisions of the 7th NSA Level meeting held in New Delhi on November 20, 2025, the statement mentioned. On Wednesday, NSA Doval expressed India's commitment to working closely with members of the CSC to enhance collective capacities in dealing with the evolving serious security challenges. In his address at the 8th National Security Advisors Meeting of the CSC in the Maldives, he said that the Colombo Security Conclave for India represents the intersection of 'Neighbourhood First' outlook and the 'MAHASAGAR' vision. "For India, the Colombo Security Conclave represents the intersection of our Neighbourhood-First outlook and the MAHASAGAR vision, which stands for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Areas. We are committed to continue working closely with the CSC countries to enhance our collective capacities in dealing with the evolving serious security challenges," he said. ( IANS)

stories.title: Indian exporters urge early US trade deal, cite proposed 17% tariff advantage
stories.summary: With US orders picking up, exporters say an early agreement would help Indian businesses protect competitiveness and secure greater market access
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Indian exporters on Thursday urged the government to seal a trade pact with the US at the earliest, saying the proposed 17 per cent tariff, as outlined in the USTR report, would give India an advantage over competing nations.
They said that this is the right time to finalise the deal as exporters are getting good orders from the US buyers.
“India should do the trade deal as soon as possible.
We are getting a lot of orders from the US, and further opening of the market will help increase exports,” Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) President S C Ralhan said.

He added that the absence of a trade deal with the US could hurt India’s exports by putting domestic exporters at a disadvantage compared with competitors from countries that enjoy lower tariff rates.
This could affect the price competitiveness of Indian goods in the US market, making it difficult for exporters to retain existing buyers and secure new orders, Ralhan said.

He added that the agreement should be balanced and reciprocal, safeguard India’s long-term economic and developmental interests, and ensure that Indian exporters can compete on a level playing field with suppliers from other countries in the US market.
“While the industry is concerned with these developments as it raises uncertainty, there is no panic amongst exporters,” he said.
Ralhan also called for clarity on how the proposed measures would interact with existing duties under Sections 301 and 232 and how the product-specific exemptions in the USTR notice would apply.
“Clear rules on the duties payable on each product would help exporters quote prices with confidence and avoid overlapping tariff burdens,” he said.
FIEO urged negotiators to secure competitive tariff treatment for Indian products, address non-tariff barriers and improve market access.
It called for particular attention to MSMEs, which have less room to absorb sudden increases in duties and compliance costs.
